home.faq1Q: Mes fichiers sont-ils envoyés sur un serveur ?
home.faq1A: Non. Tout le traitement se fait dans ton navigateur. Tes fichiers ne quittent jamais ton appareil et ne sont envoyés ni à nos serveurs ni à des tiers. C’est vrai pour chaque outil FileFlip : images, PDF, vidéos et archives sont gérés en local.
home.faq2Q: Quelle est la taille maximale des fichiers ?
home.faq2A: Les limites dépendent de la mémoire de ton appareil et du navigateur. En pratique, des fichiers de quelques centaines de mégaoctets passent souvent ; des fichiers très lourds (par ex. plus d’1 Go) peuvent ralentir le navigateur ou saturer la mémoire. En cas de limite, essaie des fichiers plus petits ou par lots.
home.faq3Q: Ça marche sur iPhone et Android ?
home.faq3A: Oui. FileFlip fonctionne dans le navigateur mobile (Safari sur iPhone, Chrome ou autre sur Android). Tu ouvres le site, tu choisis un outil et tu envoies un fichier depuis la galerie ou le gestionnaire de fichiers. Aucune app à installer. L’usage est le même que sur ordinateur, adapté à l’écran.
home.faq4A: Non. FileFlip a besoin d’une connexion internet pour charger le site et les scripts. Une fois la page chargée, le traitement des fichiers se fait dans le navigateur et n’a pas besoin d’une connexion continue pendant la conversion. Il faut être en ligne pour ouvrir et utiliser les outils.
home.faq5Q: Comment convertir un HEIC en JPG ?
home.faq5A: Va sur l’outil « HEIC en JPG » depuis la page d’accueil. Envoie un ou plusieurs fichiers HEIC (par ex. depuis ton iPhone). L’outil les convertit dans le navigateur et tu peux télécharger chaque JPG ou tout en un ZIP. Pas de compte ni d’envoi sur un serveur. La qualité reste bonne pour un usage courant.
home.faq6Q: FileFlip est-il sûr pour des fichiers confidentiels ?
home.faq6A: Oui. Comme tout se fait dans le navigateur, tes fichiers ne sont jamais envoyés à nos serveurs ni stockés par nous. Pour plus de confidentialité, utilise FileFlip sur un appareil que tu contrôles et ferme l’onglet quand tu as fini. Nous ne collectons, ne stockons ni n’analysons le contenu de tes fichiers.
home.faq7A: Non. Tu peux utiliser tous les outils FileFlip sans t’inscrire ni te connecter. Ouvre le site, choisis un outil, envoie ton fichier et télécharge le résultat. Nous ne demandons pas d’email, de mot de passe ni de données personnelles. L’usage reste simple et discret.
home.faq8A: Oui. FileFlip est gratuit, sans frais cachés ni formules payantes. L’objectif est d’offrir des outils simples et utiles à tous. Nous n’ajoutons pas de filigrane aux résultats et ne demandons pas de paiement. Tu peux utiliser les outils autant que tu veux, sans frais.

compressImage.dropzonePrompt: Glisse ton image ici ou clique pour choisir
compressImage.editorialTitle: Pourquoi compresser les images, quand utiliser JPG, PNG ou WebP, et comment choisir la qualité
compressImage.editorialBody:
La compression d’image réduit la taille des fichiers en supprimant ou en simplifiant une partie des données, pour que tes photos prennent moins de place et se chargent plus vite. Des images plus légères signifient des sites plus rapides, des pièces jointes plus faciles à envoyer et moins de soucis avec les limites de taille des formulaires ou des réseaux sociaux.

Choisis le format selon l’usage : le JPG convient le mieux aux photos et images complexes — il garde le fichier léger avec une perte visuelle minime. Le PNG conserve chaque pixel et gère la transparence, donc idéal pour les logos, captures d’écran ou graphiques aux bords nets. Le WebP offre souvent les fichiers les plus petits à qualité similaire et est supporté par tous les navigateurs récents ; utilise-le pour le meilleur compromis taille/qualité sur le web.

Le curseur de qualité règle l’intensité de la compression : des valeurs plus hautes (ex. 80–90) gardent plus de détails et des fichiers plus lourds ; des valeurs plus basses (ex. 50–60) réduisent plus la taille mais peuvent introduire des artefacts visibles. Pour la plupart des photos, 70–80 est un bon point de départ — vérifie l’aperçu et ajuste jusqu’à ce que le résultat te convienne et que la taille réponde à tes besoins.

compressImage.faq1Q: How do you compress an image online?
compressImage.faq1A: Upload your photo (JPG, PNG or WebP) using the button, choose a quality level with the slider, then click compress. You can compare the original and compressed result side by side before downloading. Everything runs in your browser, so no data is sent to any server.
compressImage.faq2A: Compression always involves a trade-off between file size and quality. You control this with the quality slider: lower values give smaller files but more visible loss. We recommend trying 60–80 for a good balance. The preview lets you check the result before downloading.
compressImage.faq3A: You can upload and compress JPG (JPEG), PNG and WebP images. The compressed output keeps the same format as the original. These formats cover the vast majority of photos and graphics used on the web and in apps.
compressImage.faq4Q: Are files saved on the server?
compressImage.faq4A: No. All processing happens in your browser. Your images are never uploaded to our servers or stored anywhere. You stay in full control of your files from start to finish.
compressImage.faq5Q: Is there a file size limit?
compressImage.faq5A: There is no fixed limit set by the tool. Practical limits depend on your device and browser memory. Very large images (e.g. tens of megabytes) may take longer to process or, on low-memory devices, cause the browser to slow down. For typical photos (a few MB), there are no issues.
compressImage.faq6Q: What is the difference between JPG and PNG in compression?
compressImage.faq6A: JPG uses lossy compression: it discards some detail to achieve much smaller file sizes, which makes it ideal for photos. PNG uses lossless compression: it keeps every pixel intact but produces larger files, and is better for graphics with sharp edges or transparency. For photos on the web, JPG usually gives the best balance of size and quality; use PNG when you need transparency or exact reproduction of logos and UI elements.
compressImage.faq7Q: How do I compress images for WhatsApp?
compressImage.faq7A: WhatsApp automatically compresses photos when you send them, which can reduce quality. To keep control, compress your image first with this tool at a quality you choose (e.g. 75–80), then send the result: the file will be smaller and may be altered less by WhatsApp. Use JPG for photos; avoid sending huge originals so the app does not apply its own heavy compression. The tool runs in the browser, so you can do it quickly from your phone or computer before sharing.
compressImage.faq8Q: Can I compress multiple images at once?
compressImage.faq8A: Yes. You can add several images in one go: use the upload button and select multiple files, or drag and drop a batch. Each image is compressed separately and you can adjust quality per image if needed. When you are done, download each file individually or use the option to download all as a ZIP. Processing runs in your browser, so there is no limit imposed by the tool—only your device memory for very large batches.
compressImage.faq9A: No. Lossy compression (as used for JPG and WebP at lower quality) permanently removes some image data; you cannot restore the exact original from the compressed file. If you might need the full quality later, keep a copy of the original before compressing. PNG compression is lossless, so the image can be decoded back to the same pixels, but the file size reduction is smaller. This tool does not store your files, so always keep your originals on your device if you want to revert.
compressImage.faq10Q: What is the best format for photos on the web?
compressImage.faq10A: For most photos on websites and blogs, JPG is still the best choice: it gives small file sizes and good visual quality at 75–85% quality. WebP often produces even smaller files at similar quality and is supported by all modern browsers; use it when you want faster page loads. PNG is better for images with transparency or sharp graphics. Save photos as JPG or WebP for hero images, galleries, and thumbnails; use PNG for logos and graphics with transparent backgrounds.

mergePdf.editorialTitle: Quand et pourquoi fusionner des PDF
mergePdf.editorialBody: Fusionner des PDF est utile quand tu as plusieurs documents — rapports, scans ou formulaires — que tu veux réunir en un seul fichier pour partage ou impression. L’outil conserve la qualité d’origine de chaque PDF et te permet de définir l’ordre en glissant les fichiers. Tout se fait dans le navigateur, tes documents ne quittent jamais ton appareil.

mergePdf.faq1Q: How do I merge PDFs online?
mergePdf.faq1A: Click the button to add one or more PDF files from your device. They appear in a list below. Drag the rows to change the order of the documents. When you are happy with the order, click "Merge PDF" to create a single PDF and download it. The process runs entirely in your browser, so your files never leave your device.
mergePdf.faq2A: You reorder whole documents, not individual pages. Drag the file rows up or down to set the order in which each PDF appears in the merged file. The pages of each PDF keep their internal order; the merged PDF is document 1's pages, then document 2's, and so on. If you need to reorder single pages within a PDF, you would need a separate tool that supports page-level editing.
mergePdf.faq3Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
mergePdf.faq3A: No. Merging is done locally in your browser. Your files never leave your device or get stored on our servers. This keeps your documents private and secure. You can merge sensitive or confidential PDFs without any upload.
mergePdf.faq4Q: Is there a limit to how many PDFs I can merge?
mergePdf.faq4A: There is no fixed limit in the tool. Very large numbers of files or very big PDFs may make the browser use a lot of memory and take longer. For typical documents (e.g. a few dozen PDFs of a few MB each), merging works without issues. If you hit performance limits, try merging in smaller batches and then merging the resulting PDFs.
mergePdf.faq5A: No. The tool combines the existing content of your PDFs without re-encoding or re-compressing the pages. Text and images in the merged PDF stay at the same quality as in the originals. The output is a single PDF that behaves like one continuous document.
mergePdf.faq6Q: Can I remove a file from the list before merging?
mergePdf.faq6A: Yes. Each file in the list has a remove or delete option so you can take it out before clicking Merge. Reorder the remaining files as needed, then merge. If you change your mind, add the file again and adjust the order.
mergePdf.faq7Q: What happens to bookmarks and links in the PDFs?
mergePdf.faq7A: Bookmarks and internal links from the original PDFs are preserved in the merged file where the library supports it. Very complex PDFs with nested bookmarks may have simplified structure in the result. External links and hyperlinks generally remain clickable in the merged PDF.
mergePdf.faq8A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser (Safari on iPhone, Chrome or others on Android). You can add PDFs from your device or cloud storage, reorder them, and download the merged file. No app install is required; processing happens in the browser so file size limits depend on your device's memory.
mergePdf.faq9A: Password-protected (encrypted) PDFs must be unlocked first before this tool can read them. Open the PDF with the correct password in another app, save it without password protection, then use that copy here. The merge tool itself does not ask for or handle PDF passwords.

heicToJpg.label: HEIC en JPG
heicToJpg.metaTitle: HEIC en JPG en ligne gratuit
heicToJpg.metaDescription: Convertir HEIC en JPG. Un ou plusieurs fichiers, aperçu, télécharger en ZIP.
heicToJpg.editorialBody: HEIC est le format photo par défaut sur iPhone et occupe moins d’espace, mais beaucoup de sites, d’apps et de destinataires attendent du JPG. Convertir en JPG rend tes photos faciles à partager et à ouvrir partout. L’outil fonctionne dans le navigateur, tes photos ne quittent jamais ton appareil.
heicToJpg.faq6Q: Does it work on iPhone and iPad?
heicToJpg.faq6A: Yes. Open the tool in Safari (or another browser) on your iPhone or iPad, then tap to add HEIC photos from your camera roll or Files app. The conversion runs in the browser and you can download each JPG or a ZIP. No app install is required.
heicToJpg.faq7A: Basic metadata such as date taken can be preserved when the conversion is done in the browser, depending on the library used. For full EXIF (camera model, GPS, etc.) preservation, some tools may strip or simplify it when encoding JPG. If you need exact EXIF, check the output or use a dedicated desktop tool.
heicToJpg.faq8A: The converted JPG keeps the same dimensions (pixel width and height) as the original HEIC. Only the format and compression change; resolution is not reduced. You get a standard JPG that you can use for print or web at the same size as the source.
heicToJpg.faq9Q: Can I convert HEIC to PNG or WebP instead?
heicToJpg.faq9A: This tool converts HEIC to JPG only. JPG is the most widely supported format for sharing and is sufficient for most uses. If you need PNG (e.g. for transparency) or WebP, you would need to convert HEIC to JPG first, then use another tool to convert JPG to the desired format, or use a converter that supports HEIC to PNG/WebP directly.
